default.reason: dev-models: a cheap fable scout classifies the aspect first, then rules route by tier -> fable (fast/cheap), opus-4.8 (the balanced strong coder), opus-ultracode (Opus 4.8 in exhaustive multi-agent orchestration). Unmatched normal-implementation dev work -> opus-4.8, the T1 floor.

plan.reason: destructive/irreversible tool call (delete): the security-release floor never drops to the cheap tier however small the call looks -> the most careful ultracode route (tierpolicy T0 floor beats latency/complexity)

caller tagged the aspect high-risk (push / release / migration / a security or policy surface): irreversible, outward-facing work takes the T0 ultracode route -> exhaustive orchestration with adversarial verification, never the cheap tier

ultra-hard / long-horizon / wide dev work (large refactor, migration, cross-cutting design, deep debugging) -> Opus 4.8 in ultracode mode: the cost of exhaustive multi-agent orchestration is bought back by correctness on the hardest work (T0). Placed before the read/search rules so a high-flagged aspect escalates even when it is read-shaped
read-shaped tool call (read/inspect): cheap, low-stakes, not destructive and not flagged hard -> fable (fast); a wrong read costs a re-run, not a bad write
search / lookup tool call: cheap read-shaped work -> fable, the T2 routine tier

moderate dev work (ordinary feature / bugfix / focused edit) -> opus-4.8, the balanced strong coder. Named explicitly (a floor >= medium) so medium work lands on the T1 model instead of falling through to the low->fable rule below
low-complexity dev aspect (small mechanical edit, quick lookup) -> fable, the T2 routine tier; reached only after the medium rule, so it bands to genuinely-low work
short interactive dev turn (quick question / tiny edit, no complexity flag) -> fable for low latency
